assumptions: Retain v3 bone geometry, coordinate limits, exact coupling, knee rotation mapping, and all 740 muscle identities and maximum strengths. Restore only the declared missing left-hand skin mass/inertia by mirroring source right-hand skin geometry.

Replace parameter-dependent virtual shoulder springs/rotors and coordinate damping with relative humerus/scapula viscous damping of 0.6 N m s/rad; engineering parameter, not subject-specific measurement.
Retain actual sternoclavicular/acromioclavicular passive terms and all explicitly reported support/contact constraints.

Human middle-finger via points and fixed transmission ratios are scaled by each native PIP-DIP distance/1.22, mirrored bilaterally, and transferred to other digits. This is an engineering approximation, not a measurement of this model subject.
Source forearm and wrist routes remain. Native FDS/FDP MCP segments with inappropriate flexion behavior are replaced by published palmar via points; original distal flexor routes remain.
Extrinsic extensor MCP segments use the published dorsal EDC via points and a neutral-moment-arm cylinder; their distal source route is replaced by the declared CS/RB/UB/TS network.

MCP intrinsic routes for digits2-4 use published radial/ulnar/lumbrical points except the index FDI heads, which retain the complete native proximal insertion; digit5 retains its native hypothenar-compatible MCP routing.

Central/terminal slips wrap on massless joint-centred cylinders. Radius equals the published neutral straight-line moment arm; lateral bands remain straight. Fixed pulley transmission preserves native virtual work but does not represent sliding nodes or an elastic extensor network.
FDS and listed intrinsic optimal fibre lengths use one independently measured specimen. Both first dorsal interosseous heads use the same46mm whole-muscle value. Remaining muscle laws are retained.

Listed fibre laws use an independently fixed all-neutral, inactive, optimal-fibre reference with rigid tendons and zero pennation. Maximum forces remain unchanged; the active runtime passive law is declared in handElasticity. No reference ratio was tuned to fixture success.
The offset of a weighted branched path is not an anatomical tendon slack length; the calibrated lengthrange is an encoding interval, not a geometric extremum.
Measured free-response damping is a population estimate and does not model activation-dependent impedance. All hand/wrist rotor armatures are zero while body inertia is retained.

Left-hand skin capsule omission is repaired by exact local geometric reflection of all source right-hand skin capsules, using unchanged density and dimensions. This restores19 homologous body masses and inertias.
Native contacts remain disabled by the engine. Existing explicit grasp contact proxies are retained; their mirrored left geometry is equivalent to the restored native left skin.

All740 actuator identities, maximum forces, normalized active laws, joint limits and coupling remain. This remains a modified research model with incomplete soft tissues and non-unique muscle recruitment.
All four available index transmission ratios are fixed to the EMBC2014 cadaver-calibrated values before testing; no ratio optimization is performed here.
Both first-dorsal-interosseous heads retain their native proximal insertion. This excludes direct distal oblique-wing transmission, not every anatomical connection to the proximal interosseous hood.
An/Synek geometric via points and native FDI path are retained. The EMBC2014 optimized via points are unavailable as numeric coordinates, so this is an explicit hybrid approximation.
Ratios concern the index finger only and are mirrored bilaterally; other digits retain their declared human-middle transfer. Input strength and neutral normalized fibre length are unchanged.

For the 36 reference-calibrated hand MTUs, override only the passive law with the published Thelen2003 defaults e0=0.6 and kpe=5 through a checked native USER-bias callback. Fmax, active force-length and force-velocity laws remain native. This is a hybrid rigid-tendon research model, not a complete Thelen muscle model.

The 24 finger-flexion coordinates include a fixed-reference aggregate passive correction using Tsakonas stiffness and Kamper reference angles. It is reported separately in N m, not as isolated ligament or joint-capsule force. Its target identity applies at unit muscle strength only.
Legacy length calibration is historical provenance. Current path/length changes require their own v4 verification.
This is a modified research model with declared anatomical approximations, not a human muscle-force measurement or a complete soft-tissue model.

parameterSources.used: Index-specific FDI proximal insertion and complete published EDC/EI/FPI/LUM force ratios. Source validation was static with gravity omitted; no dynamic validation is inherited.
Human middle-finger via points and intrinsic/extrinsic fixed tendon split; Tables 2 and 4.
Sarcomere-normalized optimal fibre length of FDS and measured intrinsic muscles; single male left-arm specimen.
Neutral inactive reference inspires fibre=optimal reference; rigid tendon and zero pennation are explicit adaptations, not direct reuse of the 1.033 divisor.
Participant-mean free-response viscous damping for each digit and joint, N m s/rad; thumb values unchanged.
Mirror every existing right-hand skin capsule to restore left-hand omitted soft-tissue mass/inertia.

passiveLaw.energy: For lambda>1: Fmax*L0*e0/kpe*(expm1(x)-x)/expm1(kpe), x=kpe*(lambda-1)/e0; otherwise zero
passiveLaw.scope: All 36 hand MTUs whose physical optimal fibre length was independently reference-calibrated; no selection by failed muscle/frame
passiveLaw.activeLaw: Unchanged native MuJoCo gain, active length curve and force-velocity curve
passiveLaw.strength: All Fmax unchanged; tested scene multipliers equal one
passiveLaw.referenceCorrection: Same fixed 24-coordinate aggregate linear specification; subtract reference passive MTU torque using these same new laws
limitations: Rigid tendon and zero pennation retained
This is a hybrid model using the published passive law only, not a complete Thelen muscle implementation
Generic published parameters are not subject-specific measured finger properties
No parameter, reference angle or fixture sweep
passiveLaw.nativeVerification: Set only selected actuator bias types to USER in the isolated process and provide the exact passive callback; active gain remains native MUSCLE

referenceCorrection.equilibriumEvidence: Kamper 2002 initial MCP/PIP/DIP 14/7/7 degrees, described as mean zero-static-torque angles; text transcription, not Table 2 polynomial
referenceCorrection.referenceRule: All independent coordinates fixed to immutable source defaults except the 24 declared current finger flexion coordinates; no current wrist/elbow/forearm/abduction/thumb dependence
referenceCorrection.musclePotentialSources: All 740 native MTUs; terms constant in h have zero derivative. No passive curve or maximum force changes.
assumptions: Measured whole-joint stiffness and index reference angles combined across studies
Index zero-torque angles transferred to all four digits and mirrored to the left hand
Joint-local linear stiffness used throughout the native allowed flexion domain as an explicit research approximation
Residual term is an aggregate reference correction, not independently measured capsule or ligament force
No abduction spring; reference abduction is fixed to defaults
referenceCorrection.selectionPolicy: One fixed candidate; no coefficient or equilibrium-angle sweep; inputs and solve tolerances unchanged

handElasticity.application: Frozen parameter declarations are applied to this derived geometry. Their baseXml/baseSha256 describe the earlier research comparison, not this active XML. The reference MTU term uses the same 36 Thelen laws as the current pose; the older linear declaration's native-only wording is historical.
handElasticity.strengthSemantics: The reference correction stays fixed at unit strength. Scene strength and individual muscle multipliers scale actual active and passive muscle forces only; the target reference identity is claimed only when all multipliers equal one.
